notes: Tiers are derived from PVI and incumbency (backtest/data/pvi.py derive_rating), not published ratings.
Only races with >= $100K total spending are modeled (backtest/data/universe.py); Alaska is excluded.
floor_share uses money outside the national committees' control as reported to the FEC by the snapshot.
The spending effect is an assumption (simple_model/spending.py), not an estimate.

NRSC v. FEC (2026-06-30) struck down party coordinated-spending limits. For 2026 the FEC reports DCCC with $0 in independent expenditures and $60.9M in coordinated party expenditures through 2026-10-14, but only ~$5.2M of that is itemized by race in the API data, so race-level DCCC spending to date is incomplete. The win probabilities do not depend on it; any --extra allocation does.

The D-incumbent coefficient (~9-11 margin points) is estimated mostly from incumbents in their own districts; for incumbents on heavily redrawn 2026 maps (e.g. TX-28, TX-34, NC-01, OH-09) it is probably overstated.
Map status: Texas (new map, SCOTUS Dec 2025) and Missouri (2022 map, SCOTUS 2026-09-25) were checked after July 2026; other redrawn states follow The Downballot's July 2026 data.
